newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 30.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Bulgaria introduces on July 1 a fixed exchange rate regime known as a currency board, which has been prescribed by the International Monetary Fund as a last chance for the Balkan country to pull itself out of a severe economic crisis.

The launch of the system will not involve cutting of ribbons and champaigne. It will involve that levs in circulation and commercial banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank match central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves, effectively pegging the lev at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 to the mark.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved amendaments to the Penal Code aimed at speeding up the legal procedure and improving the legislature for fighting organised and white-collar crime.
-- The Supreme Court ruled in favour of a central bank appeal against a lower court's rejection of an insolvency claim against First Private Bank (FPB).
The Supreme Court returned the insolvency case against the FPB for reconsideration to the Sofia City Court and recommended to declare the bank insolvent.
The FPB, Bulgaria's biggest private bank, was put in receivership on May 17, 1996 and the central bank sought its insolvency through the Sofia City Court two weeks later.
-- Bulgaria expects some 600 billion levs in proceeds from privatisation by the end of this year, under a 1997 privatisation programme reviewed by parliament's economic committee last week.
-- Bulgaria's fertilizer producers Chimko posted $35 million profit in 1996, up from $22 million the previous year, its management said.
-- The South Korean Daewoo Corp could outbid Austria's Reiffeisen Bank in the sale for Bulgaria's Expressbank.

-- Bulgaria's industry minister Alexander Bozhkov said his country planned to privatise 40 percent of its state enterprises by the year-end and added that he hoped that at least 20-25 percent of them would be sold to foreign buyers.

-- Bulgaria's Post Banks, one of the country's biggest state-owned commercial banks, said it was to raise its capital to 10 billion levs from the current 2.421 billion levs at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting due in September. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
